title: Team Task Packet
description: The frozen truth of one assigned task: what an Agent is allowed to rely on. Nothing here may change without restating the task.

schemaVersion.description: 2 replaced v1's inert `validation: string[]` with a `validationPlan` of real checks. A version bump rather than a tolerated addition because the two cannot coexist honestly: a reader that accepted both could not tell a task with no checks from one whose checks it did not understand, and would have to guess which of those means "safe to merge".

inputs.description: Declared semantic dependencies. Only id+revision are hashed into inputSnapshotDigest; authority records who can resolve the revision and is deliberately excluded from the digest.

validationPlan.description:
How this task will be shown to be done (plan §6). Replaces v1's `validation: string[]`, which was a list of commands nobody ran and nothing checked against — validation by remembering to.

At least one check, because a task that declares no way to be verified cannot be verified, and "we'll know when we see it" is the state this whole layer exists to end.

The plan is inside the frozen half on purpose, and that is what makes the rest of the mechanism trustworthy: an Agent cannot add a check that passes, drop one that fails, or edit the command it is judged by. Changing the plan means restating the task under a new generation, which is visible to everyone.

What freezing does not do is make a check safe. It proves integrity — this is the check that was agreed — and integrity is not authority: a frozen dangerous command is still a dangerous command, and the packet author is not necessarily more trusted than the subject on that axis. So a `command` check carries argv and is spawned without a shell, and a check that genuinely needs a pipeline or a substitution has to say `shell-command` and be read as such.
